scorecard.rationale: The Parkinson figure shows a small inverse tile for unspecified egg frequency and falls without a precise estimate or poaching identity. The older-adult study reports 2.03 versus 2.21 weekly portions in fall-with-fracture cases and controls with unadjusted p=.07, and has no adjusted fall-frequency or preparation-specific estimate. Nutri-Park used protein timing. The new European nutrition review includes raw egg vitamin D composition and population food-source contributions with no egg-specific fall outcome. These results leave poached eggs and Parkinson fall frequency open. An additional laboratory source uses homogenized egg yolk as an assay matrix and measures lipid peroxidation after an unrelated plant extract. It does not inform the direction of poached egg and falls. An egg-recipe trial adjusted for baseline performance imbalance and found no clear physical-function contrast. Whole eggs in a higher-protein diet yielded body-composition measurements without falls. A dried egg-white pilot listed fall counts in its registry, but the registry has no posted results and the author abstract provides no fall comparison. The near-zero Parkinson figure and the separate unadjusted fracture case-control contrast remain weak inverse observations without a poaching or fall-frequency bridge. Infant feeding interviews identify egg introduction and parental allergy concerns, without a poached-egg group or fall outcome. The apparent sea-urchin egg result concerns a separate laboratory material. The controlled older-adult fall-count gap remains.
